tasks.title: Restore Add phase and zero-phase recovery
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A roadmap without phases cannot be structurally recovered in the current workspace.

**Finding**
Phase creation and zero-phase recovery were absent from the workspace.

**Scope**
Add one canonical phase factory/mutation; wire visible toolbar, zero-state, and end-of-list creation actions; respect owner/editor/viewer modes; persist local and synced edits; record activity; focus the new phase.

**Acceptance criteria**
A zero-phase owner/editor can create a phase by keyboard, pointer, and touch; viewers get an explanatory read-only state; new phase survives reload/sync and creates one attributed activity event.

**Validation / gate**
Unit and component tests for factory/mutation/permissions/focus; browser smoke for local and synced paths; regression test deleting the final phase then recovering.

**Implementation status**
Automated implementation is complete. Factory, mutation, zero/filtered/viewer states, visible native-button actions, duplicate activation protection, expansion, focused naming, local write-through, aggregate autosync wiring, and `phase.created` activity are implemented. Four focused test files pass with 14 tests; lint and typecheck pass. Remaining gate: browser smoke must verify keyboard/pointer/touch activation, reload persistence, synced save/realtime activity attribution, and final-phase deletion recovery in a real browser session.

**Risk**
Without this, destructive phase deletion can strand an editable roadmap.

**Evidence**
`roadmap-factory.ts`, `usePhaseMutations.ts`, `usePhaseCollapse.ts`, `Workspace`, `WorkspaceToolbar`, `PhaseList`, `PhaseNameEditor`, activity display/count handling, and focused RF-016 tests.

**Classification**
confirmed

tasks.title: Make phase settings and color overlays viewport-safe
tasks.desc:
**Why**
A structural action must remain usable at narrow widths and zoom.

**Finding**
The phase menu and color controls previously used clipped in-tree absolute overlays without collision or focus management.

**Scope**
Adopt a small shared anchored-menu/popover foundation only where it replaces this duplicated behavior; migrate phase settings/color first and define layering/scroll ownership.

**Acceptance criteria**
Menu and popover remain within viewport at narrow desktop, mobile, and 200% zoom; Escape/outside click work; trigger regains focus; keyboard semantics and focus order are correct.

**Validation / gate**
Component tests plus browser screenshots/interaction smoke at narrow viewport and 200% zoom; manual screen-reader check.

**Implementation status**
Automated implementation is complete. `AnchoredOverlay` portals fixed-position content, flips and clamps to the viewport, limits height, repositions on resize/scroll/content changes, and owns outside/Escape dismissal, initial focus, focus return, menu arrow/Home/End navigation, and dialog Tab trapping. Phase settings and color controls use the primitive, mobile/touch triggers remain visible, layer order is tokenized, card overflow workarounds are removed, and custom color state follows the active phase. Ten focused interaction/position tests pass; lint and typecheck pass. Remaining gate: browser screenshots and interaction smoke at narrow viewport/mobile/200% zoom plus a manual screen-reader semantics check.

**Risk**
Overlay regressions can clip structural actions or make keyboard users lose context.

**Evidence**
`AnchoredOverlay`, anchored-overlay CSS and layer token, `PhaseSettingsMenu`, `Phase`, `phase.css`, and focused overlay/menu tests.

**Classification**
confirmed

tasks.title: Make phase mutation persistence and activity consistent
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Participants need truthful, useful history for structural changes.

**Finding**
Create was the only fully attributed structural phase mutation; other phase changes were missing events or used legacy reorder vocabulary, and an edit landing during an in-flight autosync could retain acknowledged activity or miss its retry.

**Scope**
Define canonical phase mutation/activity vocabulary and no-op rules; make local/synced persistence and attribution consistent without duplicate events.

**Acceptance criteria**
Create, rename, delete, reorder, color, and color-mode each produce at most one useful activity event when changed and none for no-ops; synced save retains the events.

**Validation / gate**
Focused mutation/activity tests and two-session manual check.

**Implementation status**
Automated implementation is complete. Phase mutations emit `phase.created`, `phase.updated`, `phase.deleted`, or `phase.reordered` with useful field and phase metadata; unchanged, missing, duplicate, and malformed operations emit nothing. Pending activity now acknowledges only the object references captured by a successful request, preserves newer edits, and retries a debounce blocked by an in-flight save. Activity labels and batch counts cover the canonical vocabulary while legacy reorder display remains compatible. Twenty-five focused frontend tests pass; lint, typecheck, and direct validation of all six backend phase actions pass. A database-backed API regression is prepared but requires the repository test PostgreSQL service. Remaining gate: run that API test and verify attribution, save, and realtime refresh in the manual two-session check.

**Risk**
Missing or duplicate structural history undermines collaboration recovery.

**Evidence**
`usePhaseMutations.ts`, `activity-changes.ts`, `useAutoSync.ts`, `useSaveFlow.ts`, `ActivityPanel.tsx`, and focused web/API regressions.

**Classification**
confirmed

tasks.title: Protect destructive final-phase and empty-workspace paths
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Destructive actions must never leave an editor without a recovery route.

**Finding**
Recovery actions existed after phase creation work, but the delete confirmation did not identify the final-phase recovery path, viewer empty phases did not explain task restrictions, and menu-to-dialog focus could land on the dialog container instead of the safe action.

**Scope**
Specify final-phase confirmation/recovery, empty-phase first-task action, filtered-empty action, and owner/editor/viewer copy.

**Acceptance criteria**
Every editable empty state has a relevant action; every viewer state explains why editing is unavailable; final-phase deletion has an immediate recovery path.

**Validation / gate**
Component tests for empty states and browser smoke across roles.

**Implementation status**
Automated implementation is complete. Delete confirmation accurately reports top-level tasks and subtasks, identifies final-phase deletion, and names Create first phase as the recovery action. Its menu-to-alertdialog handoff reliably focuses Keep phase; buttons have explicit non-submit types and Escape remains safe. Empty phases expose Add first task to editors and explain the viewer restriction; zero-phase and filtered-empty states retain distinct create/reset actions based on the unfiltered roadmap phase count. Twenty-nine focused interaction and accessibility tests pass; the full Wave 1 web gate passes 404 tests, lint, typecheck, and production build. The API gate is environment-blocked by the unavailable local test PostgreSQL service. Remaining gate: browser smoke across owner/editor/viewer states, including final-phase deletion and recovery.

**Risk**
A recoverability failure is a Beta blocker even if data deletion is confirmed.

**Evidence**
`PhaseSettingsMenu`, `ConfirmDialog`, `PhaseEmptyState`, `PhaseList`, `Workspace`, and focused empty/destructive-state tests.

**Classification**
confirmed

tasks.title: Establish a visible primary-action hierarchy
tasks.desc:

**Finding**

**Scope**

**Acceptance criteria**

**Validation / gate**

**Implementation status**

Add phase remains the first emphasized action in Roadmap view and stays available from Team view, while contextual search/filter/tag/expansion controls remain Roadmap-only. Empty/filter states keep task-specific recovery, no-op expansion controls are hidden, local Activity is focusable with a visible after-save explanation, mobile Add phase owns a full row, and rename/settings/reorder affordances retain visible low-emphasis defaults without hover. Twenty-three focused role, interaction, and accessibility tests pass; lint and typecheck pass. Remaining gate: responsive browser smoke at desktop, narrow, mobile, touch, and 200% zoom.

**Risk**
Controls may become hidden rather than clarified if redesigned without role-state coverage.

**Evidence**
`WorkspaceToolbar`, `Workspace`, `WorkspaceHead`, phase/roadmap/toolbar CSS, and the focused action-matrix tests.

**Classification**

tasks.title: Truthful save, error, offline, and session recovery states
tasks.desc:
**Why**
Users must distinguish local save, server sync, validation, conflict, and expired session outcomes.

**Finding**
Typed classification existed, but queued server edits reported Live during debounce, validation and unexpected failures had no stable attention state, connectivity could fail silently in autosync, and some forbidden paths revoked a valid session as if it had expired.

**Scope**
Map save states and messages across local and server roadmaps; preserve drafts; remove generic/misleading errors; document deliberate limitations.

**Acceptance criteria**
No network condition is described as synced incorrectly; validation differs from connectivity; retry/reload/keep-local outcomes preserve user input.

**Validation / gate**
Focused hook tests and manual fault-injection browser matrix.

**Implementation status**
Automated implementation is complete. Server-backed unsaved work reports Saving during debounce/in-flight work; validation, permission, and unexpected failures report Save needs attention; connection failures report Offline; conflicts remain distinct; and only expired/unauthorized sessions clear credentials. Autosync, manual save/reload/keep-local, and task patch flows provide outcome-specific messages and explicitly preserve local edits or task drafts. Retry/review actions remain available, newer in-flight edits remain queued, and existing idle-render/caret tests cover stable typing. Twenty-nine focused save, error, task-draft, and caret tests pass; lint and typecheck pass. Remaining gate: manual browser fault injection for connection loss/recovery, validation, 403, expiry, conflict reload, and keep-local across local and synced sessions.

**Risk**
Incorrect status can cause accidental loss or false confidence.

**Evidence**
`roadmap-sync-errors`, `useAutoSync`, `useSaveFlow`, `useTaskPatch`, sync status/indicator/header components, and controlled failure tests.

**Classification**
needs verification

**Acceptance criteria**
A first-time user can find where data lives, create phase/task, export, save/share, understand roles/locks/conflicts, restore a version, and report a problem. Selecting the RoadForge template deep-clones the canonical JSON into an independent roadmap, resets runtime/export metadata, preserves its registered tags, and cannot mutate the source through user editing. No separately maintained hard-coded roadmap can drift. CI validates the canonical file through RoadForge's real parser and strict template invariants. **Implementation status**
